title: hotfix(shadow-runner): fix worker lifecycle leak causing RSS growth + add regression test
author: Emily Zhao
release_notes: Fixes shadow-runner worker lifecycle bug that could leak per-request resources under load, causing RSS growth and eventual OOM/restarts during beta load tests. Adds regression test exercising repeated worker start/stop + high-volume shadow executions.
body:
Context: During beta load tests (and one customer-reported window in SUP-18457), shadow-runner workers showed steady RSS growth over ~20–35 minutes at moderate sampling. Queue depth stayed stable but GPU utilization and node memory pressure climbed until kube restarted pods. Heap snapshots and logs pointed at worker lifecycle paths: a per-worker JudgeClient / ModelSessionPool was being created per shadow execution in one code path and never closed, and the worker shutdown hook was not awaited when the supervisor restarted a worker after transient dequeue errors. This is a hotfix targeting the release branch used for beta.

What changed: 1) Worker lifecycle: make ShadowWorker implement explicit start()/stop() and ensure the supervisor always awaits stop() on restart and on pod termination (SIGTERM). The stop() path now drains in-flight tasks up to a timeout, then hard-cancels remaining tasks and closes long-lived resources. 2) Resource ownership: move JudgeClient + TokenizerCache + ModelSessionPool construction to worker startup (singletons per worker) and ensure close() is invoked exactly once. 3) Fix leak: remove a code path that created a new JudgeClient when judge scoring was disabled (feature-flag off) due to an inverted condition; this created an unused client per request that held onto a gRPC channel + internal buffers. 4) Backpressure safety: on dequeue failure, do not replace the worker immediately; instead mark the worker unhealthy, exponential backoff, and reuse the same worker instance (prevents rapid spawn/teardown loops that amplified leaked objects). 5) Observability: add shadow_runner.worker_restart_count and shadow_runner.worker_shutdown_timeout_count counters so we can detect lifecycle churn early.

Regression test: Adds a stress/regression test that (a) spins up a ShadowRunner with a mocked queue + mocked model target, (b) runs 25k shadow executions with scoring toggled on/off, (c) forces 50 worker restarts via injected dequeue errors, and (d) asserts that process RSS stabilizes within a small bound (we measure delta in heap-used + native allocated via the runtime metrics exported by the worker). This test failed consistently before this PR (unbounded growth) and passes now.

Risk/rollout: This is intentionally minimal and isolated to shadow-runner. It does not touch primary-path request handling. The shutdown/drain timeout defaults to 3s (configurable) to avoid long pod termination delays. After merge, SRE will roll this to beta regions first with sampling capped (per existing budgets) and watch RSS + restart counters.

Follow-ups: - Cherry-pick to main after release branch deploy (separate PR). - Consider moving JudgeClient to a shared pool with bounded concurrency (ENG follow-up). - Add an alert on worker_restart_count rate and shutdown_timeout_count > 0 for any 15m window.

Refs: incident notes from beta load test run + SUP-18457; aligns with SRE ask for lifecycle counters; complements earlier queue backpressure work.
commits: shadow-runner: make worker lifecycle explicit; await stop on restart
shadow-runner: fix inverted judge client creation condition; close resources on stop
tests: add shadow runner worker lifecycle regression/stress test
conversation:
Sean Gallagher (SRE): Can you confirm we’re not waiting indefinitely on shutdown? We had pods stuck Terminating once already.

Emily Zhao (author): Yep—stop() drains with a hard timeout (default 3s, config: shadow_runner.worker_shutdown_drain_timeout_ms). After that we cancel remaining tasks and close clients. Added metric shadow_runner.worker_shutdown_timeout_count so we can page if we ever hit it.

Vikram Singh: The JudgeClient creation bug—why was it creating clients when scoring disabled?

Emily Zhao (author): In worker.ts, the guard was inverted: if (!scoringEnabled) initJudgeClient(). That path was introduced when we added a “no-op scorer” and missed the condition. This meant every request still constructed the gRPC client (and channel) but never used it.

Logan Wright: Any telemetry cardinality changes?

Emily Zhao (author): No new tags; just two counters with worker_id already bucketed. We reuse existing service/region dimensions.

Rafael Mendes: Please add a note in the release checklist / runbook about watching RSS and the new counters.

Emily Zhao (author): Added to CHANGELOG in this PR; I’ll follow up with a runbook edit in a separate doc-only PR to keep this hotfix tight.

Sean Gallagher: Approved if perf-canary is green.

CI re-run: shadow-runner tests initially flaked due to tight RSS thresholds on shared runners; adjusted to use heap-used + native alloc metrics with a wider bound and it’s stable now.

Approvals: Sean Gallagher (Approved), Vikram Singh (Approved), Logan Wright (Approved).

Merged via squash into release/2025-11-shadow-beta. SRE to deploy to us-east + eu-west beta clusters first, then expand.
